description: CTE parsing edge cases: a definition with no column list keeps the inner projection's columns; a definition WITH a column list renames them; RECURSIVE runs to its stop condition; and a CTE resolves inside INSERT, inside an UPDATE's SET-clause subquery (including the correlated form) and inside a DELETE's IN-list. AS is REQUIRED in a CTE definition - live-Snowflake verified, the AS-less form is a sqlglot-corpus artifact and not Snowflake syntax - and the parenthesised form after the name is a COLUMN LIST only when AS follows it. Converted 1:1 from query/CTEParsingTest (now retired); the Java looked up its renamed columns through getColumnIndex, which the converted test states as an explicit column-name expectation instead.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE test_table (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (1, 'A')
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (2, 'B')
WITH cte AS (SELECT * FROM test_table) SELECT * FROM cte ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE test_table (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (1, 'A')
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (2, 'B')
WITH cte (id, val) AS (SELECT * FROM test_table) SELECT * FROM cte ORDER BY id
WITH RECURSIVE cte AS (SELECT 1 as n UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM cte WHERE n < 5) SELECT * FROM cte ORDER BY n
CREATE TABLE test_table (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (1, 'A')
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (2, 'B')
CREATE TABLE target (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO target WITH cte AS (SELECT * FROM test_table WHERE id = 1) SELECT * FROM cte
SELECT id, value FROM target ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE test_table (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (1, 'A')
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (2, 'B')
CREATE TABLE target (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO target VALUES (1, 'X')
UPDATE target SET value = (WITH cte AS (SELECT id, value FROM test_table WHERE id = 1) SELECT value FROM cte WHERE cte.id = target.id)
SELECT id, value FROM target ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE test_table (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (1, 'A')
INSERT INTO test_table VALUES (2, 'B')
CREATE TABLE target (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO target VALUES (1, 'X')
INSERT INTO target VALUES (2, 'Y')
DELETE FROM target WHERE id IN (WITH cte AS (SELECT id FROM test_table WHERE id = 1) SELECT id FROM cte)
SELECT id, value FROM target ORDER BY id

WITH t AS (SELECT 1 AS c) SELECT * FROM t
